standard_prerequisites: derived pushforward Rf_* on modules over algebraic spaces and its right derived functor viewpoint
Grothendieck abelian categories admit K-injective resolutions by complexes of injectives
the uniform vanishing bound N of the quasi-coherence direct image lemma
truncation short exact sequences of complexes
Leray acyclicity for bounded below complexes of f_*-acyclic objects and the injective-pushforward lemma
core_obligations: Construct a right derived extension Phi of f_* : QCoh(O_X) to QCoh(O_Y) on the whole derived category D(QCoh(O_X)) such that Phi followed by the embedding into D(O_Y) equals Rf_* on D_QCoh(O_X)
proof_roadmap: Noetherian hypotheses make f quasi-compact quasi-separated, so f_* preserves quasi-coherence
Represent K by a K-injective complex of injectives in QCoh(O_X) using the Grothendieck property, and define Phi(K) = f_* of that complex inside D(QCoh(O_Y))
It suffices to show the canonical map from f_*I to Rf_*I is an isomorphism on cohomology sheaves; fix a degree m and cut the K-injective complex by the truncation sequence at m - N - 1
The uniform vanishing bound kills the cohomology of the derived pushforward of the far truncation in degrees >= m - 1, so R^m f_*I agrees with the bounded-below case
For bounded below complexes of injectives, Leray acyclicity with the injective-pushforward vanishing identifies f_*I with Rf_*I
difficulty_reason: H2: a derived-functor comparison built from a K-injective model, a truncation reduction and Leray acyclicity; each reduction is written out with its quoted bound.
